engineChanges.change: All Georgetown values are unverified assumptions; require user to confirm zoning district, plat building lines and adopted code edition before finalizing
RS Residential Single-Family: use front 20 / side 6 / street side 15 / rear 10 ft as provisional defaults (unverified)
Use IECC Climate Zone 2A prescriptive envelope for the adopted IECC edition
Flag PE-sealed engineered slab (expansive clay east of I-35 / variable limestone and clay in the west)

Check the TCEQ Edwards Aquifer map: lots on the recharge zone (and some in the contributing/transition zones) fall under 30 TAC Chapter 213; regulated development needs an approved Water Pollution Abatement Plan, usually done at subdivision level. In west Georgetown expect UDC water-quality/impervious-cover limits and geologic assessment (karst features, setbacks from sensitive features).
Require tree survey; keep footprint and driveway out of critical root zones of Heritage (>= ~26 in DBH) and Protected (>= ~12 in DBH) trees, or add mitigation cost
Add Georgetown water + wastewater impact fees (Georgetown Utility Systems; amounts depend on service area and plat date) - expect several thousand USD; transportation impact fee status unknown
Most new homes are in PUDs/MUDs or HOA subdivisions - plat building lines, PUD standards and deed restrictions may override district setbacks and add masonry rules
Provisional: set front-loaded garage door >= 25 ft from front property line / street ROW

plainLanguage: This Georgetown file is unverified - our research tools were unavailable, so treat every number as a placeholder. Georgetown uses a Unified Development Code; most new homes are in the RS district or in a planned development with its own rules. Western Georgetown sits over the Edwards Aquifer, which can add water-quality rules and limits on paved area. Georgetown protects large trees, so a tree survey is often needed before you can place the house. Expect water and sewer impact fees of several thousand dollars. The city cannot require brick, but your HOA may.
